sections.name: The Carney case
sections.baseline: Jamey Carney, a 43-year-old American citizen from New York (Westchester County, according to one report; unconfirmed), had lived in Killarney, County Kerry, since about 2021 with her teenage daughter. She was killed in her home on the Muckross Road on the night of 6 July 2026, and her daughter found her body the next afternoon. The police believe that her boyfriend, Ahmad Al-Saqar, a 28-year-old Jordanian, left Killarney by bus early on 7 July and flew from Dublin to Istanbul before the body was found. He went on to Jordan, where the Public Security Directorate arrested him within days, and a Jordanian court ordered his detention. In August, according to the Irish Times, the Director of Public Prosecutions directed that he be charged with her murder; other reports say only that the DPP supported an arrest warrant. Ireland and Jordan have no extradition treaty, so his return would require a special arrangement between the two governments. Jordan could also try him itself (one report; unconfirmed). As of 23 September, he remained in custody in Jordan, talks between the two countries were continuing, and no extradition hearing had been set. No later development has been reported.

sections.name: Trenton
sections.about: Signs of natural life and revival in the city of Trenton, New Jersey: things that private people and businesses start on their own, without subsidy. That means new restaurants, shops and galleries; private home buying and renovation; small developers; rents and sale prices that show demand; new residents; and cultural or community activity started by citizens. Government action is included only when it improves the conditions for private initiative, for example lower taxes or fees, faster permits, easier zoning, clear title to vacant lots or better safety. Subsidized or politically driven projects are left out or labeled. Edition of 16 October 2026, covering about April to October 2026.

sections.baseline: Natural private revival in Trenton is still thin. The city had an estimated 91,506 residents in 2025, a median household income of $52,537 and a poverty rate of 21.6 percent (Census Bureau). Its 2025 effective property tax rate, 3.468 percent, is the highest in Mercer County, compared with 2.434 percent in Hamilton and 1.814 percent in Princeton (New Jersey Treasury), and that burden falls directly on anyone who buys, builds or rents. Much of the city's land is tax-exempt, and state aid supplies about half of the city's main operating revenue (Moody's), so most of what is announced as development is government-driven. The unsubsidized signs that do exist are modest: home prices rising, small citizen-run cultural spaces, and private firms using cheap land at the city's edge. The backgrounder judges city policy by whether it makes private initiative easier.

sections.name: France presidential election
sections.about: Tracker for the French presidential election of April–May 2027: dates, candidates, polls, Polymarket odds, and news that affects the political situation in France (the government, the budget, censure motions, candidate moves and court cases). First edition: 16 October 2026, covering about 2 to 16 October 2026.
baseline: Dates. The Council of Ministers fixed the dates on 1 July 2026: the first round is on Sunday, 18 April 2027, and the second round on Sunday, 2 May 2027. Voters in Guadeloupe, Martinique, French Guiana, Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, Saint-Barthélemy, Saint-Martin and French Polynesia vote one day earlier. The formal decree that convenes the voters has not yet been published; it must appear at least ten weeks before the first round, that is, by about 7 February 2027. If no candidate wins more than half of the votes cast in the first round, the two leaders meet in the second round two weeks later.

Getting on the ballot. A candidate needs at least 500 signed sponsorships (parrainages) from elected officials, chiefly mayors, but also members of parliament, departmental and regional councilors and others. The 500 must come from at least 30 departments or overseas territories, with no more than one tenth from any one of them. The forms are sent out after the decree is published, and the deadline is calculated to fall on about 12 March 2027 (a calculation from the law, not yet an official date). The Constitutional Council then publishes the official list of candidates and the names of the sponsors.
Macron. Emmanuel Macron, elected in 2017 and re-elected in 2022, cannot run, because the Constitution limits a president to two consecutive terms.

Candidates. National Rally (RN): Marine Le Pen, who announced on 7 July 2026 that she will run for a fourth time, with Jordan Bardella as her heir if she cannot. The center and Macron's former camp: Édouard Philippe (Horizons, declared since September 2024) and Gabriel Attal (Renaissance, declared in May 2026). The Republicans (LR): Bruno Retailleau, designated by the party in April 2026; David Lisnard, mayor of Cannes, also declared, in March 2026. Radical left: Jean-Luc Mélenchon (La France insoumise), declared in May 2026. Social-democratic left: Raphaël Glucksmann (Place publique), who won the joint primary of the Socialist Party, Place publique and the Gauche républicaine et socialiste on 11 October 2026 with 66.2 percent. Others tested in polls or declared include Éric Zemmour or Sarah Knafo (Reconquête), Fabien Roussel (Communists), Marine Tondelier (Greens), Nicolas Dupont-Aignan, Nathalie Arthaud, François Ruffin, Dominique de Villepin, the essayist Natacha Polony (declared 14 October 2026), and former president François Hollande, who has not ruled out a run. The month in which Philippe and Attal declared is taken from summaries and is unconfirmed.

Polls. Every recent poll puts Le Pen far ahead in the first round, and the race is for second place. OpinionWay (13–14 October, after the left's primary; 978 registered voters): Le Pen 35 to 37 percent depending on the centrist candidate, with Mélenchon at 14 to 15, Glucksmann at 13 to 16 (up four to five points) and Philippe at 12 to 15 (his lowest in the series); in the second round Le Pen beats Philippe 56 to 44, Glucksmann 56 to 44 and Mélenchon 68 to 32. Ifop-Fiducial for LCI and Sud Radio (12–14 October, 1,390 people): Le Pen 34, Mélenchon 16, Philippe 14, Glucksmann 14, Attal 6 in the central scenario; without Attal, Philippe rises to 18. Odoxa (published 14 October): Le Pen 37 to 38, Mélenchon about 18, Philippe 17. Toluna Harris Interactive (12 October): Le Pen 37, Mélenchon 19. Elabe for BFMTV (26–28 August, the latest Elabe vote-intention poll): Le Pen 34 to 35.5, and she would beat Philippe only narrowly in the second round, 52.5 to 47.5, a much closer result than OpinionWay's in October. The Odoxa and Harris figures come from poll aggregators, not from the pollsters' own reports, and are unconfirmed in detail.

Parliament and government. Since the snap elections of July 2024 the National Assembly has had no majority. The National Rally is the largest group, with about 118 to 119 of the 577 seats; the government's base (Renaissance/EPR, Horizons, the Democrats/MoDem and LR) is split and well short of a majority, and 289 votes bring down a government. Sébastien Lecornu has been prime minister since September 2025; his second government survived two censure motions on the 2026 budget in January 2026 (the La France insoumise motion received 269 votes). He presented the 2027 budget on 1 October 2026, again without a majority, and may have to use Article 49.3, which would expose him to a censure vote, or budget ordinances, which have never been used.

Le Pen's case. On 31 March 2025 a Paris court convicted Le Pen of embezzling European Parliament funds to pay party staff and banned her from office for five years with immediate effect, which would have kept her out of the race. On 7 July 2026 the Paris Court of Appeal upheld the conviction but cut the ban to 45 months, of which 30 are suspended. It ruled that the 15 months to be served had already run since 31 March 2025, so she is eligible. It also sentenced her to three years in prison, two suspended and one to be served with an electronic tag, and a fine of 100,000 euros. She appealed to the Court of Cassation, which suspends the sentence, including the tag. Her lawyers' written arguments were due by 15 October 2026. No hearing date has been set; a ruling is expected before the first round, possibly in early April 2027 (unconfirmed).

items.text: The Kan public broadcaster published a Kantar poll on Sunday evening (552 respondents, margin of error 4.2 points). Yashar has 22 seats, Likud 20, Bennett's Beyachad 12, Otzma Yehudit 9, and the Democrats, Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism and the Joint List 8 each. Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael and Yoaz Hendel's Reservists both cross the threshold with 4 seats. The Netanyahu bloc, counting Winter, rises from 51 to 53 and the anti-Netanyahu bloc falls from 52 to 50, with the Arab parties at 13. Eisenkot still leads Netanyahu 43% to 38% on who is more suitable to be prime minister, and 30% of respondents are undecided (Haaretz). Thursday's Zman Yisrael poll had the opposite result, 55 to 51 for the anti-Netanyahu bloc, so the polls agree only that neither side reaches 61. Winter's vote share matters most: when he crosses the threshold, the right gains about four seats, and when he falls below it, those votes are lost.
items.headline: Kan poll puts Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, the opposition at 50

items.lead: Also on Sunday, Bennett told a conference of the religious Zionist paper HaDor that Netanyahu could join a future government, and even be a minister, if he accepted the bloc's guidelines, including a state commission of inquiry into 7 October.
items.text: Also on Sunday, Bennett told a conference of the religious Zionist paper HaDor that Netanyahu could join a future government, and even be a minister, if he accepted the bloc's guidelines, including a state commission of inquiry into 7 October. Eisenkot, Yair Golan and Avigdor Liberman rejected the idea at once, and Bennett withdrew it the same evening, saying it was meant to show the absurdity of the idea. Benny Gantz was the only one to support it, calling for a unity government with Likud (Times of Israel). Shas and United Torah Judaism signed their expected surplus-vote agreement. A UTJ candidate, Moshe Rosenthal, said the party would sit with whoever passes a draft-exemption law that the High Court will uphold, and that the rabbis will decide after the election (Times of Israel). That statement leaves the door open to Eisenkot, which is a real threat to Netanyahu, because without the Haredi parties his bloc has no path to a majority.

items.lead: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent, Pierre Ghanem, reported on Sunday that the State Department intends to announce progress this week on the three-way framework between the United States, Lebanon and Israel.
items.text: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent, Pierre Ghanem, reported on Sunday that the State Department intends to announce progress this week on the three-way framework between the United States, Lebanon and Israel. According to his sources, Secretary of State Rubio has told his staff to finish two things by the middle of this month: a monitoring and verification mechanism for the "pilot zones" in the south, where Hezbollah is to be disarmed in exchange for Israeli withdrawal, and a framework for an economic aid conference for Lebanon. The main obstacle is the composition of the monitoring force. Israel objects to several countries, France in particular, and the United States will not send its own soldiers to the south, so Washington is looking for a way to use French troops away from the border alongside other European forces. A State Department official said any international presence must be tied to the goals of the framework agreement and not become "permanent mediation." The same sources say Hezbollah has raised at least $40 million a month this year through smuggling across the Syrian border, falsified transactions at the port of Beirut and state salaries, since Iran stopped sending money (Al Arabiya, via Infinity News). The American position, stated in public after Rubio met Prime Minister Salam two weeks ago, is that disarmament must come before any Israeli withdrawal.
items.headline: Al Arabiya: Washington to announce progress on the Lebanon framework this week

items.lead: An-Nahar reported new details on the 500 kilograms of explosives (250 of TNT and 250 of C-4) seized at Dahr al-Baidar.
items.text: An-Nahar reported new details on the 500 kilograms of explosives (250 of TNT and 250 of C-4) seized at Dahr al-Baidar. According to leaked investigation records, the two detained men admitted that they belong to Hezbollah and that the explosives are Hezbollah's. They said an official in the Bekaa gave them the load to deliver to the southern suburbs of Beirut, to a man known as "Dhu al-Fiqar." Judge Claude Ghanem, the government commissioner at the Military Court, sent the file back to the army's Military Police for further questioning. The paper says the idea of an assassination plot is still only a suspicion. In recent days the army has also seized 245 kilograms of TNT smuggled from Syria and another load of explosives and shells near Qasr in the Hermel district (An-Nahar). If the confessions hold up, the state will have a court case that ties Hezbollah directly to explosives moved inside Lebanon. That gives Salam something concrete to show Washington before the Tampa meeting, but it also makes a confrontation with Hezbollah harder to avoid.
items.headline: An-Nahar: detained men say the Dahr al-Baidar explosives belong to Hezbollah

items.lead: Lula held his largest rally of the campaign on Sunday on the Avenida Paulista in São Paulo.
items.text: Lula held his largest rally of the campaign on Sunday on the Avenida Paulista in São Paulo. It filled twelve blocks, the largest crowd the left has gathered there since the protests against Jair Bolsonaro, with smaller events in 76 other cities. There was no official crowd count, because the campaign did not authorize the drone flight that the USP/Cebrap monitor uses. Lula spoke mainly to young voters. Flávio Bolsonaro met Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, Mayor Ricardo Nunes and local mayors and council members at a lunch in the same city. He told them to avoid a mood of "already won" and said "nothing is settled." Tarcísio and Nunes announced a pro-Flávio rally on the Paulista next Sunday, 18 October. On the same day the president of the TSE, Brazil's Superior Electoral Court, which polices campaign content, Kassio Nunes Marques, ordered the suspension of "Exército do Lula," a WhatsApp channel with more than three million followers run by Deputy André Janones, at the request of Flávio's campaign. A few hours later the court's chief inspector, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, restored it, finding the evidence insufficient (Folha).
items.headline: Lula holds his largest rally; Flávio Bolsonaro warns allies that "nothing is settled"

items.lead: El País reports that Colombia's interior minister, Rodrigo Lara, spoke at last Wednesday's 7 October memorial at the Centro Israelita in Bogotá, the first time the national government has attended.
items.text: El País reports that Colombia's interior minister, Rodrigo Lara, spoke at last Wednesday's 7 October memorial at the Centro Israelita in Bogotá, the first time the national government has attended. He said Colombia would take relations with Israel "to levels never seen before" and that he had met Yehuda Kaploun, Trump's special envoy against antisemitism, two days earlier. George Levy, president of the Confederation of Jewish Communities, called the De la Espriella government "the best friend of the Jewish people in the world." Graffiti has appeared on the building of the Israeli embassy and on a kosher restaurant in Bogotá (El País). The embassy in Jerusalem opens on Wednesday 14 October at 6:30 p.m., with Foreign Minister Omar Bula and Gideon Sa'ar presiding (Caracol Radio). Colombia will be the tenth country with an embassy in the city. Marcos Peckel of the Jewish Confederation told El País that the coal trade is symbolic and that the strategic part is security, cyber, counter-drone systems and intelligence, along with Colombia's vote on the UN Security Council.
items.headline: Colombia's government turns toward Israel; Jerusalem embassy opens 14 October

items.text: Speaking by video at the X Takeover fan event in Texas on Saturday, Musk said that Starship Flight 15 will try to catch the upper stage with the launch tower, which would be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket, and that he hopes it will fly in four to six weeks, "a little bit before Thanksgiving." These are his claims. SpaceX has not published a mission plan, and the FAA, which licenses every launch and reentry, has not changed the license. NASASpaceflight notes that the current license covers only the Flight 14 reentry, and that changing the mission profile to a ship catch could take time to approve. Its unofficial schedule, taken from FAA planning slides, puts Flight 15 (Ship 42 and Booster 22, from Pad 2 at Starbase) no earlier than 8 November. Ship 42 has had its six engines removed and has gone back for a third round of pressure testing, perhaps to fix the vacuum-engine failures seen on Flights 12 and 14 (NASASpaceflight). There is nothing material on xAI or Cursor.

EU sets up a training mission for Lebanon's army and police as UNIFIL prepares to leave
items.lead: On 12 October, EU foreign ministers set up the EU Support Mission in Lebanon (EUSM Lebanon), with an initial mandate of three years.
items.text: The mission has a military part, which will advise and train the Lebanese Armed Forces on border and maritime security, and a civilian part, which will train the Internal Security Forces on cybercrime and anti-smuggling. The EU says it is not a replacement for UNIFIL, whose mandate ends at the end of 2026. Euronews reports that it will not operate in southern Lebanon. An EU official said personnel could deploy in the coming months. Rapporteur reports, citing confidential plans, that the mission will have about 100 military personnel, mostly in Beirut, with France and Italy competing to lead it; this has not been confirmed by a second source. Asharq Al-Awsat writes that the aim is to free the Lebanese army to concentrate on disarming Hezbollah.

items.headline: Grok Bot 0.70.2: Bots get their own email addresses and can search X
items.text: Version 0.70.2, released on 11 October, lets a Bot claim its own email address and receive mail there. Any email it sends from that address waits for the user's approval. Bots can now also search X and read posts without a connected X account, and some connectors, such as Figma, Notion and Canva, can appear as interactive cards in the chat. The release also lets Bots pay with X Money or Stripe Link. The official changelog is the source. The Botski Blog, an unofficial site, also reports the X search and the email feature, but it does not confirm the version number or the payment feature, which are therefore unconfirmed by a second source.

items.headline: Grok Bot 0.68: slide decks, formatted email and Gmail send-as addresses
items.text: Version 0.68.0 (5 October) lets email drafts go out from a verified Gmail send-as address and adds five languages: Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Swahili and Hausa. Version 0.68.1 (7 October) lets Bots build slide decks as PowerPoint files or Google Slides, send formatted emails, and search the Gmail Spam folder. It also enlarges the Bot's computer screen to 1920 × 1200. The official changelog, the Grok Bot Wiki and the Botski Blog all report these changes.

items.headline: Katz: if Hezbollah joins an Iranian attack, Israel will take more land around Nabatieh and the Litani
items.lead: Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Wednesday, during a visit to the IDF buffer zone in southern Lebanon, that if Hezbollah joins Iran in an attack on Israel, it will lose more territory around Nabatieh and the Litani River as part of a permanent Israeli security zone.
items.text: Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Wednesday, during a visit to the IDF buffer zone in southern Lebanon, that if Hezbollah joins Iran in an attack on Israel, it will lose more territory around Nabatieh and the Litani River as part of a permanent Israeli security zone, and that the IDF is prepared for an expanded invasion. He also said another evacuation of the Dahiyeh district of Beirut would follow, and that more than one million Shiites would be displaced. The Jerusalem Post notes that this is the first specific Nabatieh threat from Katz in several months, and that many of his election-season threats have not led to major new operations. Israel already holds a strip of southern Lebanon up to about 10 kilometers from the border (Jerusalem Post; This Is Beirut).

items.headline: Quaest's first runoff poll: Flávio 46%, Lula 44%, a technical tie
items.lead: Quaest's first national runoff poll, published on Wednesday for Globo and O Globo (2,154 interviews, 10–13 October, margin of error 2 points), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 46% and Lula at 44%.
items.text: Quaest's first national runoff poll, published on Wednesday for Globo and O Globo (2,154 interviews, 10–13 October, margin of error 2 points, TSE registration BR-08729/2026), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 46% and Lula at 44%, a technical tie. One percent are undecided and 9% say blank, null or will not vote. Rejection is almost equal: 54% say they would never vote for Flávio and 53% for Lula. Ninety-one percent say their choice is final. Compared with Quaest's pre-first-round runoff scenario, both candidates rose by two points as blank and null fell. On Polymarket Flávio is at about 84% and Lula at about 16%, down slightly for Flávio from about 86% on 12 October. The runoff is on 25 October; the Band debate is on 18 October and Globo's on 23 October (G1; Exame; Polymarket).

items.headline: Colombia opens its embassy in Jerusalem; Sa'ar and Bula preside
items.lead: Colombia inaugurated its embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday 14 October, becoming the tenth country with an embassy in the city.
items.text: Colombia inaugurated its embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday 14 October, becoming the tenth country with an embassy in the city. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar and Colombian Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar unveiled the sign; Sa'ar affixed a mezuzah. Sa'ar said that when he took office there were five embassies in Jerusalem and that President Abelardo de la Espriella had kept a campaign promise to move Colombia's mission there. Bula said relations "should never have been broken" and called Israel a strategic partner. Ambassador Tania Gilinski will head the mission. The free-trade agreement, cancelled under Gustavo Petro, was restored the day before. The Palestinian Authority and Jordan condemned the move (Israel National News; Al Jazeera / AFP).

items.headline: Cursor opens an Origin App Marketplace with more than 20 partner apps
items.lead: On 13 October Cursor's changelog announced an Origin App Marketplace with more than 20 apps for deployments, CI, code review, security, monitoring and project management.
items.text: On 13 October Cursor's changelog announced an Origin App Marketplace with more than 20 apps for deployments, CI, code review, security, monitoring and project management. Named partners include Cloudflare, Netlify, Render, Spacelift and Vercel for deployments; Buildkite, CircleCI and others for CI; CodeRabbit, Greptile and Tenki for code review; Artemis Security, Semgrep, Socket Security and Upwind for security; Sentry for monitoring; and Linear for project management. Public submissions are open: teams build against the Origin API, submit a slug, tags and a demo video, and Cursor reviews before listing. There is nothing new on the official Grok Bot changelog since version 0.70.2 (11 October), already reported, and nothing material on SpaceX beyond the Flight 15 catch claim already covered on 12 October (Cursor changelog).

items.headline: Parti Québécois MNAs to be sworn in today; cabinet due 21 October
items.lead: The 59 newly elected Parti Québécois members of Quebec's National Assembly are to be sworn in on Thursday 15 October; Liberal opposition members on 19 October; and the PQ cabinet on 21 October.
items.text: The 59 newly elected Parti Québécois members of Quebec's National Assembly are to be sworn in on Thursday 15 October; Liberal opposition members on 19 October; and the PQ cabinet on 21 October (Radio-Canada; CBC). Premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says he will not swear an oath of allegiance to the King, relying on Quebec's 2022 law that made the National Assembly oath the only required oath. That law is under court challenge; an injunction hearing is expected between 19 October and 9 November. St-Pierre Plamondon has asked government lawyers whether he can keep his campaign pledges to bar the lieutenant-governor from the opening speech and to redirect the lieutenant-governor's office budget (about 1.3 million Canadian dollars for 2026–27) to homelessness work. Governor General Louise Arbour has said she is skeptical of those plans (CBC; Radio-Canada).

items.headline: Zman Yisrael poll: Yashar 26, Likud 20; blocs still 54–49
items.lead: A Zman Yisrael poll for the Times of Israel, fielded on 14–15 October (500 respondents, margin of error 4.4 points), gives Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar 26 seats and Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud 20.
items.text: A Zman Yisrael poll for the Times of Israel, fielded on 14–15 October (500 respondents, margin of error 4.4 points), gives Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar 26 seats and Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud 20. The anti-Netanyahu Jewish-led bloc has 54 seats and the Netanyahu bloc 49, both short of 61, with Arab parties at 13 and the nonaligned Reservists at 4. Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael is at 2.8%, below the 3.25% threshold. Last week's Zman Yisrael split was 55–51 the other way on the blocs; the party gap between Yashar and Likud has widened from 24–20 to 26–20 (Times of Israel).

items.headline: Channel 13 Madad poll: Netanyahu bloc 51, Eisenkot 50; Hendel and Winter both at 4
items.lead: Channel 13's Madad poll (Shmuel Rosner and Noah Slepkov, 1,018 respondents, margin of error 3.1 points, fielded 13 October) puts Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats and Eisenkot's at 50, with Arab parties at 15.
items.text: Channel 13's Madad poll (Shmuel Rosner and Noah Slepkov, 1,018 respondents, margin of error 3.1 points, fielded 13 October) puts Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats and Eisenkot's at 50, with Arab parties at 15. Yashar leads with 20 seats and Likud has 18. For the first time in this Madad series, Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha's Reservists clear the threshold with 4 seats; Winter's Amcha Yisrael also has 4. That result conflicts with the same week's Zman Yisrael poll, which had Winter below the threshold. Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 45% to 38% as more suitable to be prime minister (Channel 13; Madad).

items.headline: Netanyahu: Defense and National Security stay with Likud; Otzma fires back
items.lead: At a campaign event in Acre on Thursday, Netanyahu said that if he forms the next government, Likud will keep the National Security and Education ministries, and repeated that Itamar Ben-Gvir will not be defense minister.
items.text: At a campaign event in Acre on Thursday, Netanyahu said that if he forms the next government, Likud will keep the National Security and Education ministries, and repeated that Itamar Ben-Gvir will not be defense minister. Otzma Yehudit accused him of planning to shut the party out of the next coalition and bring in Eisenkot instead. Ben-Gvir told Walla he still expects to become defense minister if Otzma gains seats. Friday 16 October is the legal deadline for surplus-vote agreements; Otzma remains the only party in Netanyahu's bloc without one after Ben-Gvir refused a deal with Winter (Times of Israel; Ynet).

items.headline: EUSM Lebanon: Italy, France and Spain expected to supply most of about 100 troops
items.lead: Reporting on the force plan for the EU Support Mission in Lebanon (established by the Council on 12 October) says Italy, France and Spain are expected to provide most of a permanent military component of about 100 personnel, based mainly in Beirut, with no planned deployment to southern Lebanon near the Israeli border.
items.text: Reporting on the force plan for the EU Support Mission in Lebanon (established by the Council on 12 October) says Italy, France and Spain are expected to provide most of a permanent military component of about 100 personnel, based mainly in Beirut, with no planned deployment to southern Lebanon near the Israeli border. France is pushing to lead the mission at first; Italy has already named a command candidate; command is expected to rotate yearly (Rapporteur, 9 October; details confirmed against the Council decision of 12 October). The mission advises and trains the Lebanese Armed Forces and Internal Security Forces on border, maritime and related tasks; it is not a UNIFIL replacement. On the Israeli-reaction watch: no new official statement from the Foreign Ministry, the Prime Minister's Office or the IDF responding to EUSM itself was found since yesterday's edition.

items.headline: Datafolha: Flávio 47%, Lula 45% in the runoff, still a technical tie
items.lead: Datafolha's runoff poll for Folha de S.Paulo, published on Thursday (2,520 interviews on 13–14 October, margin of error 2 points, TSE registration BR-00466/2026), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 47% and Lula at 45%.
items.text: Datafolha's runoff poll for Folha de S.Paulo, published on Thursday (2,520 interviews on 13–14 October, margin of error 2 points, TSE registration BR-00466/2026), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 47% and Lula at 45%. Among valid votes the split is 51% to 49%. A week earlier Datafolha had Flávio at 49% and Lula at 45%; the gap has narrowed. The poll is the first Datafolha after large pro-Lula street events. Rejection is 46% for Lula and 44% for Flávio (G1; Folha).

items.headline: All 59 PQ MNAs sworn in; cabinet still due 21 October
items.lead: On Thursday 15 October, all 59 Parti Québécois members of Quebec's National Assembly were sworn in at the Red Room in Quebec City, taking an oath of allegiance to the people of Quebec rather than to the King.
items.text: On Thursday 15 October, all 59 Parti Québécois members of Quebec's National Assembly were sworn in at the Red Room in Quebec City, taking an oath of allegiance to the people of Quebec rather than to the King. Premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon spoke of the party's largest caucus since 1998 and said cabinet, of about 20 ministers, is still due on 21 October. Liberal MNAs are to be sworn in on Monday, Québec solidaire on Tuesday and Conservatives on Thursday. A court challenge to the 2022 law that dropped the oath to the King remains pending (Canadian Press via CityNews; Radio-Canada).

items.headline: Israel Hayom poll: change bloc 52, right 50; Yashar 24; Winter still below the threshold
items.lead: An Israel Hayom / Kantar poll published on Thursday (551 adults online, 14–15 October, margin of error 4.2 points) puts the change bloc at 52 seats and the right at 50.
items.text: An Israel Hayom / Kantar poll published on Thursday (551 adults online, 14–15 October, margin of error 4.2 points) puts the change bloc at 52 seats and the right at 50. Yashar rises to 24 from 22 in the prior Israel Hayom survey; Likud has 21; Bennett's Beyachad falls one seat to 12. Otzma Yehudit has 9 and Religious Zionism 6. Hendel–Zelekha's list has 4; Winter's Amcha Yisrael remains under the electoral threshold. The paper notes that neither Jewish-led camp reaches 61 without some form of Arab-party involvement, and that 87% of change-bloc voters in the survey would accept joining, external support, or abstention by an Arab party (Israel Hayom).

items.headline: Lieberman rules out a minority government and Arab or Haredi partners
items.lead: On Thursday Avigdor Lieberman told a conference of the Israel Democracy Institute that Yisrael Beytenu would oppose any minority government and demanded a majority coalition of Zionist parties only.
items.text: On Thursday Avigdor Lieberman said Yisrael Beytenu would oppose any minority government, including a transitional one, and demanded a majority coalition of Zionist parties only, without Ra'am, the Joint List, Shas or United Torah Judaism. He also said his party would not sit with Likud while Netanyahu leads it. Benny Gantz replied that Lieberman was either lying about eventually relying on Arab parties or that the country was heading to a repeat election. The dispute matters because recent polls show neither Jewish-led bloc reaching 61 without Arab involvement (Jerusalem Post; Israel Hayom).

items.headline: Israel Hayom reports a U.S. push for Netanyahu–Eisenkot unity; Huckabee denies it
items.lead: Israel Hayom on Thursday described a proposed framework in which Likud and Yashar would form a broad government, with Netanyahu serving up to two years then retiring; U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee denied any U.S. effort to steer the election.
items.text: Israel Hayom on Thursday, citing diplomatic officials, described a proposed framework in which Likud and Yashar would form a broad government, with Netanyahu serving up to two years then retiring, while advancing regional deals, especially with Saudi Arabia. Eisenkot's side would seek a timed Netanyahu exit, rollback of judicial-reform laws, and an October 7 state inquiry, according to that report. U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee posted on X that the U.S. government is "NOT trying to manipulate Israel's election or telling [the PM] what to do," called related claims fake news, and Channel 14 reported the same denial (Israel Hayom; Channel 14).

items.headline: Colombia withdraws from the Hague Group after opening its Jerusalem embassy
items.lead: Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar announced Colombia's withdrawal as a member and co-chair of the Hague Group, a coalition that sought legal and diplomatic pressure on Israel over Gaza.
items.text: Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar announced Colombia's withdrawal as a member and co-chair of the Hague Group, a coalition that sought legal and diplomatic pressure on Israel over Gaza. Colombia's Foreign Ministry said on 15 October that Colombia had formally left; Bula said the group was "created to isolate and attack Israel" and that Colombia rejects that approach. Bolivia and Honduras had already left. He spoke after the 14 October embassy inauguration in Jerusalem, with Netanyahu and Gideon Sa'ar present, condemned the October 7 massacre, and criticized the prior Colombian government's record on terrorism and antisemitism. The embassy opening itself was covered on 15 October; the Hague Group exit is the new diplomatic step (Colombian Foreign Ministry; Ynet).

items.headline: SpaceXSI releases Grok Voice 3.0; tops Artificial Analysis speech-to-speech ranking
items.lead: On 14 October SpaceXSI released Grok Voice 3.0, its newest speech-to-speech model for the Voice Agent API.
items.text: On 14 October SpaceXSI released Grok Voice 3.0, its newest speech-to-speech model for the Voice Agent API. Independent benchmark site Artificial Analysis ranks it first on the Speech-to-Speech Index at 86.9, ahead of OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 83.2 and Google's Gemini 3.8 Live (Extended Thinking, High) at 82.6; Grok Voice 2.0 scored 81.3. SpaceXSI and Artificial Analysis both report about 97% on Full Duplex Bench. API price is unchanged at $0.08 per minute ($4.80 per hour). The alias grok-voice-latest now points to grok-voice-3.0. SpaceXSI says the model powers millions of Tesla in-car conversations a day and about 20,000 Starlink support calls a day (company figures). SiliconANGLE separately reported the launch and the Artificial Analysis ranking (SpaceXSI; SiliconANGLE).

items.headline: SpaceXSI launches The X Subscription, bundling Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium
items.lead: On 12 October SpaceXSI introduced The X Subscription, one plan that includes Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium.
items.text: On 12 October SpaceXSI introduced The X Subscription, one plan that includes Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium. Paid tiers are Plus ($8 a month), Premium ($30), Super ($100) and Ultra ($200), plus a free tier with limited use. SpaceXSI says Premium matches what SuperGrok, Cursor Pro and X Premium+ used to cost together at about $90 a month, and that each paid tier's shared Grok usage pool covers Grok apps, the Grok tab on X, and Cursor, with at least twice the coding usage of the comparable older Cursor plan. Existing SuperGrok, Cursor and X Premium subscribers may keep their current plans or switch when the option appears in billing settings. TechCrunch reported the same structure and prices on 13 October. The item was not in the 12–15 October digest editions (SpaceXSI; TechCrunch).

items.headline: Reports: Cursor reviewed whether employee Grok Bot testing sent confidential data toward SpaceXAI training
items.lead: On 15 October TokenPost reported that Cursor staff in late July 2026 reviewed whether use of an internal Grok Bot test tool called Sand could have put confidential customer, supplier or partner information into data shared for SpaceXAI model training.
items.text: On 15 October TokenPost and CryptoBriefing reported that Cursor staff in late July 2026 reviewed whether use of an internal Grok Bot test tool called Sand could have put confidential customer, supplier or partner information into data shared for SpaceXAI model training. According to those accounts, Cursor then required company email logins for Sand and stopped using employee-use data for future training. TokenPost quotes a Cursor lawyer in Slack as saying the company arguably lacked rights to train on that data. Both outlets say there is no publicly confirmed evidence that client or partner data was actually exposed. The review reportedly began weeks before SpaceX completed its acquisition of Cursor on 14 August 2026. Primary paywalled detail is attributed to The Information (TokenPost; CryptoBriefing).

items.headline: School protests: a mainly high-school movement, now in its fourth week, with about 8,000 people taken into custody
items.text: The movement is real and large, but it is chiefly a movement of lycéens (high school pupils, mostly aged 15 to 18), not of university students, although some universities, parents and unions have joined. It began in mid-September in the Paris suburbs (reports name Créteil and Seine-Saint-Denis) over teacher shortages, overcrowded classes and dilapidated buildings, and spread to schools across France through class strikes, blockades of school entrances and marches. Scale: the Interior Ministry counted more than 250,000 marchers on 6 October, about 71,500 on 8 October and 161,500 on 13 October (41,500 in Paris); unions claimed about 480,000 on 13 October (one source; unconfirmed). On 6 October the government reported disruption at 891 high schools, almost a quarter of all lycées; about 200 were still blockaded on 14 October. Violence: most marches have been peaceful, but clashes at the end of several marches in Paris (Bastille on 8 October, Place Vauban on 13 October), Marseille, Lyon, Nantes and elsewhere involved fireworks, stones and burning cars on one side and tear gas, water cannon and stun grenades on the other. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu told the Senate on 14 October that 937 police and gendarmes, 149 school staff and 248 pupils had been injured since the start. The Justice Ministry reported 7,950 people taken into custody (6,773 minors), 2,735 prosecuted and 26 held in pretrial detention. A 15-year-old lost a hand to a police stun grenade and a pupil in Tours lost an eye; police officers have been charged in that case and in a case at Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône, and 36 internal police inquiries are open.
items.lead: A mainly high-school movement over teacher shortages and crowded classes; about 161,500 marched on 13 October by police count; about 8,000 taken into custody, mostly minors; 937 police and 248 pupils injured.

items.headline: Who backs the protests, what each side says, and how the government has responded
items.text: Protesters and their supporters say the cause is years of underinvestment in schools, and many denounce police tactics; the CGT and student unions have called further days of action. Human Rights Watch said on 14 October that the protests were overwhelmingly peaceful and that police used excessive force against children. Critics, including the government, say a violent minority, not all of them pupils, attacks police and schools, and that La France insoumise (LFI) encourages the unrest. Lecornu spoke of 'unprecedented violence.' On 1 October Bruno Retailleau, the Republicans' candidate, said the question of banning LFI 'arises' because it 'calls for sedition'; Jordan Bardella of the National Rally proposed that the cost of the damage be split between the families of arsonists and LFI. Jean-Luc Mélenchon replied that there had been 'neither a leaflet, nor a speech, nor a call' from LFI to blockade any school, called it 'the first mass movement summoned by telepathy,' and accused Marine Le Pen's 'friends in the police' of violence. Government response: the use of one type of stun grenade was suspended after the injury of the 15-year-old, and the government says it will speed the assignment of substitute teachers (the second point is reported by TF1 only; unconfirmed).
items.lead: Unions and the left back the pupils; the government, LR and the RN blame LFI for fanning violence; Mélenchon denies organizing it.

items.headline: Public opinion and possible effect on the 2027 election: support for the pupils, rejection of LFI's role
items.text: Polls taken from 1 to 9 October agree that about half or more of the French back the pupils but want the protests to end. Elabe for BFMTV (6–7 October): 55 percent approve, 72 percent call the demands legitimate, 55 percent want the movement to stop. Cluster17 for L'Opinion (7–9 October): 57 percent support, 53 percent want it to end as soon as possible. Ifop for LCI (6–7 October): 48 percent support or sympathize, below the 57 percent recorded for the 2023 pension protests. Ipsos: 54 percent approve. Odoxa for Le Figaro (1 October): 62 percent find the movement justified, but 61 percent say LFI is out of its role and 78 percent call its involvement electoral. Support is sharply divided by party (above 80 percent on the left; about a third among RN voters; under a quarter among LR voters) and by age (above 70 percent among the young). Analysts quoted by Le Dauphiné (the sociologists Camille Peugny and Vincent Tiberj) doubt either a large rightward backlash or a large surge in young left-wing voters; Tiberj noted that voting is no longer the main outlet for many young people. The Soufan Center argues that the protests have raised Mélenchon's standing among young voters and could matter for whether he reaches the second round. The first-round polls have not shifted visibly: a Toluna Harris Interactive poll for RTL (12 October) put Le Pen at 35 to 37 percent. On Polymarket on 16 October, Le Pen stood at about 46 percent and Mélenchon at about 11.5; I have not measured how these odds moved during the protests.
items.lead: Polls: about 48 to 62 percent back the pupils, but most want the protests to end and most reject LFI's involvement; no clear movement yet in first-round polls.

items.headline: Glucksmann wins the left's primary in the first round
items.lead: On 11 October Raphaël Glucksmann, leader of Place publique, won the joint primary of the Socialist Party, Place publique and the Gauche républicaine et socialiste in the first round, with 66.17 percent (79,613 votes).
items.text: On 11 October Raphaël Glucksmann, leader of Place publique, won the joint primary of the Socialist Party, Place publique and the Gauche républicaine et socialiste in the first round, with 66.17 percent (79,613 votes). Olivier Faure, first secretary of the Socialist Party, had 14.46 percent, Ségolène Royal 7.62, Emmanuel Maurel 5.92 and Jérôme Guedj 5.83; 120,787 people voted. The vote was extended by a day after a cyberattack slowed the online platform. For the first time, the Socialist Party will not have one of its own members as its presidential candidate. Glucksmann invited François Hollande, who stayed out of the primary, to join him, and called on the whole left except La France insoumise to unite.

items.headline: Ifop: Glucksmann ties Philippe; Le Pen at 34 percent
items.lead: In an Ifop-Fiducial poll for LCI and Sud Radio (1,390 people, 12–14 October), published three days after the primary, Glucksmann and Édouard Philippe each have 14 percent in the central scenario, behind Jean-Luc Mélenchon at 16 and far behind Marine Le Pen at 34; Gabriel Attal has 6.
items.text: In an Ifop-Fiducial poll for LCI and Sud Radio (1,390 people, 12–14 October), published three days after the primary, Glucksmann and Édouard Philippe each have 14 percent in the central scenario, behind Jean-Luc Mélenchon at 16 and far behind Marine Le Pen at 34; Gabriel Attal has 6. If Attal withdraws, Philippe rises to 18 percent and would reach the second round, ahead of Mélenchon at 16. Odoxa, also published on 14 October, has Le Pen at about 37 percent, Mélenchon at 18 and Philippe at 17.

items.headline: 2027 budget clears its first vote with help from the National Rally
items.lead: On 13 October the National Assembly rejected the Socialists' preliminary motion to reject the 2027 budget, 236 votes to 149; the National Rally voted with the government.
items.text: On 13 October the National Assembly rejected the Socialists' preliminary motion to reject the 2027 budget, 236 votes to 149; the National Rally voted with the government. Had it passed, the bill would have gone to the Senate without debate in the Assembly. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu had written to the Socialists that morning asking them to withdraw the motion; they refused, saying that he will not make the richest pay more. Lecornu says this budget should be "as reversible as possible" and that tax questions belong to the presidential campaign. The Socialists have not ruled out a censure motion.

items.headline: Lecornu presents a budget without a majority and hopes for a compromise by December
items.lead: Lecornu presented the 2027 budget to the Council of Ministers on 1 October, as last year without a majority in Parliament.
items.text: Lecornu presented the 2027 budget to the Council of Ministers on 1 October, as last year without a majority in Parliament. He has three ways to pass it without a vote: Article 49.3, which would expose the government to a censure motion that needs 289 votes; budget ordinances under Article 47, never used, and not possible before 18 December; or a special law that carries the budget past 31 December. On 15 October he said that he expects to reach a compromise with members of Parliament by December. The Assembly continued to debate the revenue side that day.

items.headline: Le Pen would end financial aid to Ukraine after six months
items.lead: Marine Le Pen said on 14 October that, if she is elected, she would keep France's financial aid to Ukraine for six months and then end it, saying that France no longer has the means.
items.text: Marine Le Pen said on 14 October that, if she is elected, she would keep France's financial aid to Ukraine for six months and then end it, saying that France no longer has the means. According to reports, she would continue to supply military equipment (this distinction is not confirmed by every report).

items.headline: Le Pen's appeal to the Court of Cassation moves forward
items.lead: The deadline for the written arguments in Le Pen's appeal to the Court of Cassation passed on 15 October (1 October for the lawyers who joined first).
items.text: The deadline for the written arguments in Le Pen's appeal to the Court of Cassation passed on 15 October (1 October for the lawyers who joined first). Thirteen appeals were filed in the case. The court must now appoint a reporting judge and an advocate general and then set a hearing; no date has been announced. A ruling is expected before the first round, but the date is not confirmed. Until then the appeal suspends her sentence, including the electronic tag.

items.headline: Essayist Natacha Polony declares her candidacy
items.lead: Natacha Polony, the essayist and former editor of Marianne, announced on France Inter on 14 October that she will run, under the slogan "We are France." Her program centers on industrial and energy sovereignty, jobs, schools, public services and the fight against corruption.
items.text: Natacha Polony, the essayist and former editor of Marianne, announced on France Inter on 14 October that she will run, under the slogan "We are France." Her program centers on industrial and energy sovereignty, jobs, schools, public services and the fight against corruption. Like every candidate, she must collect 500 sponsorships.

items.headline: Polymarket: Le Pen at about 46 percent
items.lead: On Polymarket's market for the winner of the next French presidential election (about $152 million traded), Le Pen stood at about 46 percent on 16 October, followed by Édouard Philippe at about 18.5, David Lisnard and Jean-Luc Mélenchon at about 11.5 each, and Glucksmann at about 4.
items.text: On Polymarket's market for the winner of the next French presidential election (about $152 million traded), Le Pen stood at about 46 percent on 16 October, followed by Édouard Philippe at about 18.5, David Lisnard and Jean-Luc Mélenchon at about 11.5 each, and Glucksmann at about 4. A separate market on the National Rally's candidate has closed in favor of Le Pen. Note that Lisnard's price is much higher than his polls (about 6 percent).

items.headline: A citizen-run gallery on East Hanover Street, years in the making, opens its fourth show
items.text: Hanover Creative Gallery at 219 East Hanover Street, a project its founders began planning in 2019, opened in March 2026 with the textile show 'Fiber Politic' and held its ribbon cutting on 2 April. Its curator, Áine Mickey, is a local organizer who earlier assembled shows at Trenton's BSB Gallery. A new group show, 'Vicious Involution,' runs from 2 to 31 October. NJArts.net wrote that it takes courage to open an independent gallery in a city 'not known for independent galleries.' The building also houses WorkWell, a nonprofit job program. Unconfirmed: whether the gallery received any public grant; none was reported.

items.headline: Meridian Furniture, a private Trenton company, buys 10 acres for a 220,000-square-foot warehouse
items.text: On 15 September the City Council approved the sale of more than 10 acres of city land at 300 to 366 Enterprise Avenue to Meridian Furniture for $1 million. The company, founded in Trenton more than 20 years ago, will build a warehouse of about 220,000 square feet with its own money. No subsidy has been reported; the city's part was to sell unused land at a price, which returns it to the tax rolls. The city expects about 200 jobs; that figure comes only from the city. The land sale and the size of the building are confirmed by public planning records.

items.headline: Privately owned Ironhawks hockey team begins play in Trenton on 24 October
items.text: The Trenton Ironhawks, a new ECHL team, open their first season at CURE Insurance Arena on 24 October against the Adirondack Thunder and will play 36 home games. The team is owned by Pro Hockey Partners, a private group of partners led by Joe Eng. Public element: the arena itself is publicly owned by Mercer County (not independently checked for this item).

items.headline: City puts 28 abandoned buildings into private hands, with priority for buyers who will repair and live in them
items.text: From 1 to 30 October the city is taking applications from private buyers for 28 city-owned houses and buildings in all four wards. This passes the test of this section because it returns vacant property to private owners rather than spending public money on it; the repairs would be private. Many buildings need major work, and buyers who will live in them receive priority. How many private buyers apply is the real measure of demand; results have not been reported.

items.headline: Private home buyers are paying more: city reports average sale price up 5.8 percent
items.text: According to the city, Multiple Listing Service data show the average sale price of a Trenton home rose from about $226,000 in 2025 to about $239,000 so far in 2026. Unconfirmed: this is the city's own reading of the data. Redfin shows recent median sale prices near $250,000, which is consistent with rising private demand but is not the same measure.

items.headline: Maariv poll: blocs tied at 51, Likud falls to 18, Arab parties reach 14
items.lead: A Maariv poll by Lazar Research with Panel4All (700 respondents, 14–15 October, margin of error 3.7 points), published on 16 October, puts Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar at 21 seats and Likud at 18, down two from the previous week.
items.text: A Maariv poll by Lazar Research with Panel4All (700 respondents, 14–15 October, margin of error 3.7 points), published on 16 October, puts Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar at 21 seats and Likud at 18, down two from the previous week. The other parties: Bennett's Beyachad 13, the Democrats 9, United Torah Judaism 8, Otzma Yehudit 8, Yisrael Beytenu 8, the Joint List 8, Shas 7, Religious Zionism 6, Ra'am 6, Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael 4 and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists 4. The Netanyahu bloc and the Zionist opposition have 51 seats each; the Arab parties together have 14, their highest in this poll series; the Reservists (4) are not counted in either bloc, and neither bloc would reach 61 even with them. Asked what should happen if the result is inconclusive, 55 percent prefer a unity government and 27 percent another election (18 percent do not know). As prime minister, Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 48 to 41; Netanyahu and Bennett are tied at 43; Netanyahu leads Lieberman 43 to 37. The share of undecided voters was 5.2 percent.

items.headline: Channel 12 Friday poll: anti-Netanyahu parties 49 percent, Netanyahu bloc 37
items.lead: A Channel 12 poll by Midgam (Mano Geva) for the Friday program Ulpan Shishi, taken on 15 October among 503 respondents (margin of error 4.4 points), found 49 percent support for the parties opposed to Netanyahu, including the Arab parties, against 37 percent for the Netanyahu bloc, including Winter's party.
items.text: A Channel 12 poll by Midgam (Mano Geva) for the Friday program Ulpan Shishi, taken on 15 October among 503 respondents (margin of error 4.4 points), found 49 percent support for the parties opposed to Netanyahu, including the Arab parties, against 37 percent for the Netanyahu bloc, including Winter's party. Fifty-eight percent prefer a prime minister other than Netanyahu and 35 percent prefer Netanyahu. Eight percent are still undecided, but only 3.7 percent are undecided between the blocs or do not know, down from 5.4 percent in the previous poll; 77 percent say they intend to vote. In head-to-head comparisons, Eisenkot and Bennett are each seen as more trustworthy and better on security and the cost of living than Netanyahu, except among coalition voters. Asked whom they believe in the dispute between Netanyahu and the former Shin Bet head Ronen Bar, 43 percent chose Bar and 34 percent Netanyahu. This release gave vote shares by bloc, not a seat count.

items.headline: Surplus-vote deadline passes: Ben-Gvir, Winter and Hendel–Zelekha are left without partners
items.lead: The deadline for surplus-vote agreements passed at noon on Friday, 16 October (the law allowed digital filing until the end of the day, so the final list awaits publication by the Central Elections Committee).
items.text: The deadline for surplus-vote agreements passed at noon on Friday, 16 October (the law allowed digital filing until the end of the day, so the final list awaits publication by the Central Elections Committee). Five pairs were reported as signed: Beyachad with Yisrael Beytenu, Yashar with the Democrats, the Joint List with Ra'am, Likud with Religious Zionism, and Shas with United Torah Judaism. Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists signed with no one. Ben-Gvir repeated that he would not sign with Winter, whom he calls 'Bennett 2.' Hendel and Zelekha said they offered Winter a deal on condition that he commit to sit only in a 'Zionist' government and that he refused; Winter's party denied that any contact took place. A party without an agreement does not lose its surplus votes, but it competes alone for the remaining seats. Separately, voting at Israel's missions abroad has closed with a turnout of 86.7 percent, up from about 69 percent in 2022, according to the Elections Committee as quoted in the press; this is a small group of about 4,800 diplomats and staff and does not indicate national turnout.

items.headline: Hezbollah admits the seized explosives are its own and demands them back; Rubio says that is 'out of the question'
items.lead: On 15 October the Hezbollah member of parliament Hassan Fadlallah acknowledged that the explosives seized by the Lebanese army on 5 October at the Dahr al-Baidar checkpoint belong to Hezbollah.
items.text: On 15 October the Hezbollah member of parliament Hassan Fadlallah acknowledged that the explosives seized by the Lebanese army on 5 October at the Dahr al-Baidar checkpoint belong to Hezbollah. According to a judicial source, the shipment held 500 kilograms of explosives: 250 kilograms of TNT and 250 kilograms of C-4. Hezbollah demanded that the explosives be returned and that the two men detained with them be released, said the material was meant for use against Israel, and warned the authorities. Prime Minister Nawaf Salam promised firm action and noted that C-4 has been used in past political assassinations in Lebanon. Lebanon has seized three shipments of explosives since the start of October. In a phone call with President Joseph Aoun, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that returning the explosives to Hezbollah is 'out of the question' and that everyone who ordered, financed and directed the shipment should be held accountable; he also criticized Lebanon's 1955 law boycotting Israel and urged direct military-to-military communication with Israel to avoid incidents. On 16 October the IDF carried out air strikes in southern Lebanon; the Home Front Command told Galilee residents they might hear explosions, and the IDF fired an interceptor at a suspicious aerial target (no sirens sounded).

items.headline: Two new runoff polls: Flávio Bolsonaro barely ahead, within the margin of error
items.lead: Two polls published on 16 October show the 25 October runoff almost even.
items.text: Two polls published on 16 October show the 25 October runoff almost even. CNT/MDA, its first runoff poll (2,014 face-to-face interviews, 13–15 October, margin of error 2.2 points, registered with the electoral court as BR-00652/2026), gives Flávio Bolsonaro 50.5 percent of valid votes and Lula 49.5; counting all answers, 46.8 to 45.9, with 4.9 percent blank or null and 2.4 percent undecided. Fewer voters reject Flávio than Lula: 46.6 percent say they would not vote for Flávio and 48.8 percent would not vote for Lula. Futura Inteligência (2,000 interviews, 14–15 October, margin of error 2.2 points, BR-03764/2026) gives Flávio 50.8 percent of valid votes and Lula 49.2, a narrower lead than its 51.8 to 48.2 of 13 October; its rejection figures are Lula 47.2 and Flávio 46.1. Both results are within the margin of error, as was Datafolha's 47 to 45 in the previous edition.

items.headline: Colombian foreign minister ends Israel visit with Herzog; tourist visa exemption restored
items.lead: Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar ended his four-day official visit to Israel on 16 October with a meeting with President Isaac Herzog.
items.text: Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar ended his four-day official visit to Israel on 16 October with a meeting with President Isaac Herzog. According to the Colombian Foreign Ministry, they discussed cooperation in security, defense, trade, investment, artificial intelligence, agriculture and water. The two countries restored the mutual exemption from tourist visas and have designated ambassadors; the minister also visited the Old City of Jerusalem and the Western Wall. Infobae reports that Colombia has recognized Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights, which it describes as a position shared only by the United States; this was not found in the Colombian ministry's statement and is unconfirmed. Infobae calls Colombia the eleventh country with an embassy in Jerusalem, while the earlier report used here said the tenth; the correct count is unconfirmed. Infobae also reports condemnations of the visit from Iran, Egypt, Kuwait, Turkey and the Arab Parliament.

items.text: On 16 October Gabriela Castillo Madrid, head of government affairs for SpaceX's AI business, testified by video to a New York City Council hearing on AI safety, after the Council threatened to enforce a subpoena. Council Speaker Julie Menin said that she had used Grok that morning to produce a sexualized image of herself. Devin Kim, a former xAI employee who is now president of the Center for AI Safety, testified that the company had only three AI-safety staff and that his concerns had been dismissed. The Grok Bot changelog shows no new release since version 0.70.2 of 11 October.

items.headline: Electricity Authority plans a 200-megawatt cap per new data center; decision due Sunday
items.lead: Israel's Electricity Authority plans to limit each new data center to 200 megawatts and to publish the draft for three weeks of public comment, starting on Sunday, 18 October, Calcalist reported on 14 October.
items.text: Israel's Electricity Authority plans to limit each new data center to 200 megawatts and to publish the draft for three weeks of public comment, starting on Sunday, 18 October, Calcalist reported on 14 October. Requests to connect data centers to the grid total about 27,000 megawatts, against installed generating capacity of about 18,800 megawatts; average demand is about 9,000 megawatts and the record peak was 17,300 megawatts in August 2025. Fifty of the requested facilities are larger than 200 megawatts, among them Mega DC (1,100 megawatts, on the former Alliance tire factory site in Hadera) and SDS (875 megawatts, in Nesher). New applications were frozen for 140 days from June, and the authority estimates data centers could use about 20 percent of national electricity by 2030. According to reports in TheMarker and The State of Israel, members of the authority differ on the total capacity to allow through 2035, from several hundred megawatts to about one gigawatt, against requests of up to 2.3 gigawatts; proposals include construction deadlines and guarantees of NIS 2 million per megawatt, and only a partial decision is expected on Sunday.

items.headline: China lets Visa prepare a domestic card-clearing business and books its first US soybeans since the summit
items.lead: China's central bank approved on 13 October Visa's application to prepare a domestic bank-card clearing institution; Visa has one year to prepare and cannot yet issue renminbi cards.
items.text: China's central bank approved on 13 October Visa's application to prepare a domestic bank-card clearing institution; Visa has one year to prepare and cannot yet issue renminbi cards. On 15 October Qiu Wenxing of the Chinese embassy in Washington called the approval 'a direct outcome of the presidential summit' between Trump and Xi in late September. This week Chinese state-owned buyers booked at least 20 cargoes of US soybeans, about 1.3 million tons, the first purchases since the summit, according to Bloomberg as cited by Quartz; most will be loaded from December to March. US soybeans still face Chinese tariffs of about 13 percent and are not on the lists of tariff cuts; China has pledged to buy 25 million tons a year through 2028. The two leaders are due to meet again at APEC in November and the G20 in December.

items.text: On 16 October China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology proposed adding 40 technologies, in fields including artificial intelligence, biomedicine and solar power, to the catalogue of technologies whose export is restricted: 14 would be banned and 26 would need a license. items.headline: Burnham rules out a second Scottish independence referendum while he is prime minister
items.lead: On his first major visit to Scotland as prime minister, in Motherwell on 16 October, Andy Burnham ruled out a second independence referendum during his premiership; Downing Street sources said this applies to his whole time as leader.
items.text: On his first major visit to Scotland as prime minister, in Motherwell on 16 October, Andy Burnham ruled out a second independence referendum during his premiership; Downing Street sources said this applies to his whole time as leader. He offered 'deeper devolution' instead, including powers over employment support now held by the Department for Work and Pensions, and said he will meet the first ministers at the National Economic Council. The Scottish Conservative leader, Russell Findlay, criticized him. Earlier, Burnham had told MPs that a referendum would be considered if there were a clear consensus. First Minister John Swinney gives his keynote speech to the SNP conference in Aberdeen on 17 October; according to the BBC's preview, he will say that 'the stars are aligning' and that every first minister in Edinburgh, Cardiff and Belfast now supports the right to self-determination. The SNP won a fifth term in May but without a majority.

items.headline: Greenland's parliament votes to prepare a ban on deep-sea mining until 2029
items.lead: On 15 October Greenland's parliament, Inatsisartut, unanimously adopted a resolution telling the government to draft a temporary ban on deep-sea mining and exploration until 31 December 2029, which could be extended two years at a time.
items.text: On 15 October Greenland's parliament, Inatsisartut, unanimously adopted a resolution telling the government to draft a temporary ban on deep-sea mining and exploration until 31 December 2029, which could be extended two years at a time. The bill is expected in the spring 2027 session, so no binding ban exists yet. The vote came a day after President Trump said that 'massive oil, gas and mineral exploration' in Greenland was about to begin. Greenland's deputy minister for mining, Jørgen Hammeken-Holm, said the situation was 'very far away from massive,' and Denmark said the September agreement gives American investors no preferential access.

items.text: At the swearing-in of the Parti Québécois's 59 members of the National Assembly on 15 October, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon closed with 'Vive le Québec libre' but said that before talking about independence the PQ must 'get Quebec back on the rails' and regain voters' confidence, the Montreal Gazette reported. items.headline: A local developer's graffiti museum plans a five-story home on East State Street
items.lead: The American Graffiti Museum, a nonprofit founded in 2021 by the Trenton native Daniel R.
items.text: The American Graffiti Museum, a nonprofit founded in 2021 by the Trenton native Daniel R. Brenna Jr., whose firm Ajax Management Group has redeveloped more than 70 properties in the city over 25 years, plans a 100,000-square-foot museum of graffiti and street art in a five-story historic building on East State Street, with a 12,000-square-foot courtyard. The site was secured in 2022 and the building is under construction; no opening date has been set. Its 'Downtown Gets Up' events this year brought new murals by CRASH, Ron English, Wane One, Queen Andrea and the Trenton artist Leon Rainbow, and an exhibition at Hanover Creative Gallery. The founders expect 200,000 or more visitors a year; that is their own projection. Public element: the event series was paid for in part by a state grant of $210,161 from the New Jersey Economic Development Authority's A.R.T. program, funded by the federal American Rescue Plan. Funding for the building itself was not reported.

items.headline: OpinionWay: Glucksmann gains after the primary, Philippe at his lowest, Le Pen at 35 to 37
items.lead: Two OpinionWay polls taken on 13 and 14 October, after the left's primary (978 registered voters in a sample of 1,043), were published on 15 October.
items.text: Two OpinionWay polls taken on 13 and 14 October, after the left's primary (978 registered voters in a sample of 1,043), were published on 15 October. In the Présitrack poll for Les Echos and Radio Classique, Marine Le Pen has 35 percent if both Gabriel Attal and Édouard Philippe run, followed by Jean-Luc Mélenchon 14, Raphaël Glucksmann 13, Philippe 12, Attal 7 and Bruno Retailleau 7. With Attal as the only centrist, Le Pen has 37, Glucksmann 16, Mélenchon 15, Attal 11 and Retailleau 9; with Philippe as the only centrist, Le Pen has 35 and Mélenchon, Glucksmann and Philippe 15 each, with Retailleau at 8. Glucksmann gained four to five points; Philippe fell three points to his lowest level in this series. In the OpinionWay poll for CNEWS, Le Pen has 35, Mélenchon 15, Glucksmann 13 and Philippe 12 in the first round, and in the second round she beats Philippe 56 to 44, Glucksmann 56 to 44 and Mélenchon 68 to 32. Her margin over Philippe is much wider than in Elabe's August poll (52.5 to 47.5). On Polymarket there has been no material change: Le Pen about 46 percent, Philippe about 17.5, Lisnard and Mélenchon about 11.5 each, Glucksmann about 3.5.

items.headline: Lecornu: the school movement has become 'urban violence'; it weakens as the holidays begin
items.lead: On 15 October Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said that the movement 'no longer looks like a high-school movement' but like 'a movement of urban violence,' with violence increasing in Paris, Créteil and Lyon.
items.text: On 15 October Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said that the movement 'no longer looks like a high-school movement' but like 'a movement of urban violence,' with violence increasing in Paris, Créteil and Lyon. The Paris police prefecture counts 1,260 arrests in the Paris area since the start, 86 percent of them minors, with 286 police officers and gendarmes injured there. Nationally, Education Minister Édouard Geffray reported 165 school staff injured, 17 more than the day before. After his third meeting with the pupils' unions on 15 October, the USL union walked out, said it will not attend Monday's meeting, and said the mobilization will continue during the holidays and after. On 16 October, the last school day before the two-week Toussaint holidays, fewer schools were blockaded, but there were incidents: at the Paul-Éluard lycée in Saint-Denis, teachers blocked police who entered to arrest a minor, and the Bobigny prosecutor opened an inquiry into violence against police; in Lorient seven people were arrested on 15 October and two lycées were closed on 16 October; in Alsace, police used tear gas in Bischheim and a firework mortar was fired at a principal in Mulhouse. In Nantes six teenagers were arrested over a fire at the Talensac lycée; in Salon-de-Provence a 21-year-old was charged over a lycée fire that caused about €350,000 in damage; in Marseille a 15-year-old was charged over an attack on a bus.

items.headline: Saturday 17 October: a 'convergence' day against the cost of living, with bans in central Paris
items.lead: Pupils, so-called students, former gilets jaunes, climate activists, the CGT-led union alliance and the Confédération paysanne have called for a joint day of protest against the cost of living on Saturday, 17 October; the main farmers' unions, the FNSEA and the Coordination rurale, are not taking part.
items.text: Pupils, so-called students, former gilets jaunes, climate activists, the CGT-led union alliance and the Confédération paysanne have called for a joint day of protest against the cost of living on Saturday, 17 October; the main farmers' unions, the FNSEA and the Coordination rurale, are not taking part. The Socialist Party called on people to march, and Jean-Luc Mélenchon called for a gathering at Place de la République at 2 p.m. The office of Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez spoke of about 500 planned actions and more than 90 demonstrations. Estimates of the turnout differ: intelligence services expect 60,000 to 110,000 people outside Paris (BFMTV and RTL); a police source quoted by AFP expects about 150,000 outside Paris and 40,000 in Paris; the gilets jaunes announced about 1,500 actions. The Paris police prefect, Patrice Faure, banned demonstrations around the Élysée, Matignon, the Champs-Élysées, Concorde, Bastille and other sites (fine €135); the authorized route runs from République to Place de Clichy, which the student collective Interfac IDF refused, and many metro stations are closed. The stun grenades suspended for the school protests (after a 15-year-old lost a hand in Lens on 5 October) may be used again in case of 'extremely serious urban violence'; the teachers' union SNES-FSU called this irresponsible. Lecornu set up an interministerial crisis cell, Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin told prosecutors to prepare special court arrangements, and President Macron, in Brussels, appealed for calm. The government also extended to the end of the year a €100 aid for people who drive long distances to work. The website of the Republicans (LR) was hacked by activists calling for the protests; an LR source said no data was leaked.

items.headline: Opinion and analysis: 69 percent approve of the 17 October protest; an essayist doubts a repeat of 2018
items.lead: An Elabe poll for BFMTV (1,506 people, 14–16 October) finds that 69 percent of the French approve of the mobilization against the cost of living (36 percent support it and 33 percent feel sympathy; 14 percent are indifferent, 10 percent opposed and 7 percent hostile).
items.text: An Elabe poll for BFMTV (1,506 people, 14–16 October) finds that 69 percent of the French approve of the mobilization against the cost of living (36 percent support it and 33 percent feel sympathy; 14 percent are indifferent, 10 percent opposed and 7 percent hostile). Approval is 83 percent among left-wing (NFP) voters, 70 percent among National Rally voters, 55 percent among Republican voters and 51 percent among voters of Macron's camp, and 77 percent among people aged 18 to 24. Sixty-five percent say people are right to protest now rather than wait for the vote in April. AFP also cites 55 percent support for the high-school and student movement (71 percent among 18- to 24-year-olds). On the candidates: Marine Le Pen (CNews, 15 October) called for 'total transparency' in the criteria of Parcoursup, the university admissions system; Édouard Philippe proposed school days focused on the morning and shorter Toussaint and Easter holidays, and defended Parcoursup. The government says 2,000 of the 3,000 promised substitute teachers have been assigned (Education Ministry via AFP, which confirms the point reported earlier by TF1 alone) and promises Parcoursup measures before the end of October. Analysis: the essayist Jean-Laurent Cassely told RTL on 16 October that he does not expect a repeat of the 2018 gilets jaunes movement; he said the gilets jaunes and the pupils, though marching side by side, come from different social and cultural worlds, and their votes will not express the same anger.

items.headline: Protest day: clashes in Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux, Marseille and Lille; 272 arrests by 3 p.m.
items.lead: The 17 October day of protest against the cost of living brought tens of thousands into the streets and violent clashes in several cities.
items.text: The 17 October day of protest against the cost of living brought tens of thousands into the streets and violent clashes in several cities. At noon the Interior Ministry counted 140 actions outside Paris with 32,800 people. By 3 p.m. police had made 272 arrests nationwide, according to the ministry, BFMTV and Reuters; 133 of them were in Paris by 2 p.m., mostly for 'gathering with intent to commit violence.' In Paris, the police prefecture said several hundred people, 'mainly from the ultra-left,' attacked police at Place de la République from 1 p.m.; police used tear gas and a water cannon, and the authorized CGT march left for Place de Clichy at 2:30. An undeclared march toward the Élysée was turned back. A car and a newspaper kiosk were set on fire at Place de la République, AP reported, as carried by France 24. In Marseille, dozens forced their way into the city hall lobby, and a municipal police station was attacked; Mayor Benoît Payan demanded an account of the policing. In Lyon, a branch of the tourist office was ransacked and set on fire while firefighters were kept away. In Bordeaux, a march of several thousand turned into clashes. In Lille, several hundred people fought riot police beside a peaceful march, and some briefly broke into city hall. AFP, carried by Europe 1, reported about 20,000 marchers each in Lyon and Nantes and 10,000 in Rennes at 3 p.m., without naming the source of the count. The unions and organizers had not published a national figure by early evening, and the ministry had not published a final one; the organizers had expected 60,000 to 110,000. Jordan Bardella said only 'professionals of chaos' were in the streets; Marine Le Pen said the left had taken the protests hostage. Jean-Luc Mélenchon said tens of thousands marched calmly while television showed only violence. The police inspectorate is examining at least 24 complaints of police violence, Reuters reports.

items.headline: Ipespe poll: Flávio 48, Lula 46; first runoff debate on Sunday
items.lead: A third poll this week shows the runoff within the margin of error, with the gap narrowing.
items.text: A third poll this week shows the runoff within the margin of error, with the gap narrowing. Ipespe, commissioned by Abrapel and published on 17 October (1,500 telephone interviews, 13–15 October, margin of error 2.6 points, registered as BR-00223/2026), gives Flávio Bolsonaro 48 percent and Lula 46, against 49 to 44 in its previous round. In valid votes the figures are 51.2 to 48.8, down from 52.7 to 47.3. Each candidate is rejected by 47 percent. Among the 89 percent who say they are certain to vote, Flávio leads 50 to 46. Veja and CNN Brasil report the poll. The two candidates meet in their first runoff debate on TV Band on Sunday, 18 October, at 8 p.m. Brasília time (2 a.m. Monday, Israel time), according to BBC Brasil.
